newsitem.title: UK: Rio Algom to boost copper output, push costs lower.
newsitem.headline: Rio Algom to boost copper output, push costs lower.

text.p: Canadian mining firm Rio Algom Ltd plans to more than double copper output and drive down production costs over the next five years despite the sharp fall in world copper prices in 1996.

The group aims to produce over 600 million lbs (272,000 tonnes) of copper annually within the next five years from its 1996 target of around 250 million lbs (113,000 tonnes), said Rio Algom chief financial officer Mike Parrett.
"Our roots will remain in copper," Parrett said at a presentation in London on Monday.
"We view copper as a very attractive asset," he added.
Parrett said the group would focus on driving down its production costs to better cope with price cycles.
"Overall the average cost of producing copper (for Rio Algom) is 60 cents a lb ($1,323/tonne)," Parrett said.
"When all our new projects come into being we would expect the average cost of copper production to be in the low 40-cent ($882) area within the next five years," he added.
"This will help us to ride out the inevitable commodity price cycles," said Don Cumming, Algom's executive vice president, mining operations.

Rio Algom's exposure to copper prices would rise with production. In 1997 a 10-cent change in prices would affect each share by 34 cents, while in 1998 the leverage would increase to 46 cents per share, Rio Algom estimates show.
In 1996 Rio Algom hedged its copper production though put options at $1.10 a pound during the first six months of the year and $1.00 a pound in the second six months.
"There is nothing in place for 1997 so far," Parrett said.
He said that the sharp fall in copper prices this year would affect the company's profits but not its mining plans. Other copper miners may not be so lucky.
"We believe this will lead to current and future projects being abandoned," he said.

Cumming said Rio Algom would produce 125 million lbs (59,000 tonnes) of copper cathode in 1996 from its Cerro Colorado mine in Chile and a further 117 million lbs (53,000 tonnes) from its Highland Valley operation in British Columbia.
A detailed study of another expansion is underway at Cerro, possibly adding 90 million lbs (41,000 tonnes) to output.
A further 100 million lbs (45,000 tonnes) is expected to come annually from Rio's interest in the Bajo de la Alumbrera mine in Argentina by the year 1998.
The mine is expected to begin production during the third quarter of 1997.
Also on the company's agenda is the Antamina project in Peru, where output could generate an additional 200 million lbs (91,000 tonnes) production by 2001.
As well as focusing on its core copper business, Rio Algom is proceeding with the development of the Smith Ranch uranium project in Wyoming.
Rio Algom also produces coal and and some zinc, and expects to see a positive return from gold operations within 18 months.
It owns the North American Metals Distribution group, which in 1995 contributed nearly 40 percent of the company's operating profit.
Earnings from the distribution group were down in the first half of 1996 because of lower steel and aluminium prices, but volumes remained steady.
-- Mike Collett-White, London Newsroom +44 171 542 8057
